_about: Candidate context-dependent forks authored against the frozen SNA snapshot (proposal v4, Sections 3.1 and 3.4). Each pair names two options, the page passage that states each, and two spec-sheet lines: one under which each option is the documented answer. The pipeline (python -m escalate tasks) decides whether its fork check fires, which source ranks higher (that option becomes the assistant's recommendation), and whether the deciding fact survives the blind-vs-informed filter. 'selected' marks the six pairs proposed for the 12 measured tasks; the rest are backups and count toward the ~30-query candidate pool.

pairs.query: Which QoS should I use to submit this GPU job?
pairs.deciding_fact: how long the GPU job runs

options.condition: job runs longer than 24 hours, up to 3 days

rule_source.highlight: Only request the resources which your job needs, do not over-request resources.

sheet_lines.gpu_short: Stage 3, evaluation sweep: about 10 h of wall time on 1 GPU.
sheet_lines.gpu_medium: Stage 2, training: about 30 h of wall time on 1 GPU.

questions.gpu_short: Which QoS do you use for the Stage 3 evaluation sweep?
questions.gpu_medium: Which QoS do you use for the Stage 2 training run?

pairs.key_logic: A 30 h job under gpu_short (24 h limit) is terminated at its time limit (FAQ: 'runs until it ... reaches its time limit, at which point the scheduler terminates it'), so gpu_medium is the only valid option. A 10 h job fits both; the Policies page ('do not over-request resources') makes gpu_short the documented answer.
pairs.exclusivity: hard one way (30 h), policy rule the other way (10 h)
